title: Quasi-finite etale shriek preserves constructible cohomology
statement: Let $\Lambda$ be a finite commutative ring. All derived categories below are the bounded-below derived categories of sheaves of $\Lambda$-modules on the small etale sites [def-weil-pbc-derived-categories] [def-weil-pbc-direct-image]. For a separated finite-type morphism $h:T\to B$ of quasi-compact and quasi-separated schemes [def-pc-scheme] [def-weil-pbc-scheme-conventions] and a compactification $c=(j:T\hookrightarrow\overline T,p:\overline T\to B)$, with $j$ a quasi-compact open immersion and $p$ proper, set $Rh_!^c=Rp_*j_!$ [def-weil-pbc-projection-compactification] [def-weil-pbc-extension-by-zero]. Assume $h:T\to B$ is also quasi-finite [pqf-def-quasifinite] and of finite presentation. If $K\in D^+(T_{\Et},\Lambda)$ has constructible cohomology [def-weil-pbc-etale-constructible-sheaf], then $Rh_!^cK$ has constructible cohomology on $B_{\Et}$ for every compactification $c$. In particular this applies to a closed immersion of finite presentation.

source.place: Tags 0GK3, label lemma-qf-f-shriek-constructible, and 0GKM, label lemma-Rf-shriek-for-quasi-finite; finite-ring bounded-below specialization

proof.text: Apply the finitely presented Zariski main factorization to $h$: its separatedness, quasi-finiteness, finite presentation and qcqs target are precisely the hypotheses. Obtain $T\xrightarrow{a}T_1\xrightarrow{g}B$ with $a$ a quasi-compact open immersion, $g$ finite and finitely presented, $T_1$ qcqs, and $h=g\circ a$. A finite morphism is proper: apply the finite-morphism permanence statement (c) to $g$ and the proper identity of $B$. Hence $d=(a,g)$ is a compactification permitted in the statement.

Convert finite-value module constructibility to Scheme.IsConstructibleSheaf using isConstructibleEtaleModuleSheaf_iff. Apply the already proved IsConstructibleSheaf.openImmersionLowerShriek to a and its closed complement a.closedComplement, whose range is complementary by a.range_closedComplement. Quasi-compactness of a supplies the retrocompactness hypothesis in that theorem. Convert back with the same equivalence. This uses the existing open-closed stratification proof rather than rebuilding the stalk argument.

source.place: Tag 0GK3 (lemma-qf-f-shriek-constructible), separated case, open extension step; expanded using Etale Cohomology 0F70 (lemma-jshriek-open) and the constructible strata definition

proof.text: Let E be openImmersionLowerShriek along a and P be lowerStar along g. Both are exact, by extension-by-zero exactness and finite-direct-image exactness. For J=E.mapDerivedCategoryPlus.obj K, rightDerivedFunctorPlusIsoMapDerivedCategoryPlus identifies R+P(J) with P.mapDerivedCategoryPlus(J). Apply homology and compose with the inverse of P.mapDerivedCategoryPlusHomologyFunctorIso, then with P.mapIso of the inverse of E.mapDerivedCategoryPlusHomologyFunctorIso. The result is H^q(Rh_!^d K) isomorphic to P(E(H^q(K))). These are the exact-functor cohomology comparisons, valid in every integer degree for bounded-below complexes without an upper bound.

source.place: Tag 0GKM (lemma-Rf-shriek-for-quasi-finite), finite higher direct image vanishing; 0GK3 first sentence, exactness and cohomology

proof.text: Step 2 makes E(H^q(K)) constructible. Apply finite finitely presented pushforward constructibility to g, whose source and target are qcqs by the factorization. This makes P(E(H^q(K))) constructible. Apply homology to rightDerivedLowerShriekOfCompactificationPlusIso for c and d, and compose with the isomorphisms of step 3. Transfer constructibility along the inverse composite with IsConstructibleSheaf.of_iso, using the finite-value comparison at both ends. This proves the assertion for every c and q.

For a closed immersion h, Mathlib infers IsFinite h, hence local finite type, quasi-compactness, separatedness, quasi-separatedness and LocallyQuasiFinite h. For each x, h.quasiFiniteAt x and Scheme.Hom.quasiFiniteAt_iff_isOpen_singleton_asFiber give the open singleton in the fibre required by the project definition of IsQuasiFinite. Package these with the finite-type and quasi-compact instances and apply the preceding quasi-finite theorem. All coefficient, finite-presentation, qcqs and compactification hypotheses are unchanged.
